summary: Defines a YANG model for an abstract view of a provider network's topology, showing the Service Attachment Points where services such as VPNs or network slices can attach. It augments the ietf-network model of RFC 8345.

eli5.summary: A map showing the doors where customers can plug into a provider's network.

questions: where can services attach to a network
what is a service attachment point
what is the difference between a sap and a termination point
subtitle: A YANG model that lists the points on a provider network where services such as VPNs and network slices can be attached.

tldr.problem: Service providers need an abstract, machine-readable view of where services can be delivered to customers, so that service ordering, feasibility checks and coverage tracking can be automated.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-sap-ntw YANG module augments the ietf-network model of RFC 8345 so that each node lists its Service Attachment Points per service type, with identifiers, interface details, role and status.
tldr.outcome: A network controller can expose where services can be, and are being, delivered to a service orchestration layer, covering both UNI and NNI attachment points. The RFC is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 9408 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2023. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Service Attachment Points
sections.content:
Service providers offer services such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), SD-WAN overlay networks and network slices. To automate service provisioning, they need a view of where those services can be delivered to customers. That view can feed an entity that handles service orders, service feasibility checks and per-service coverage tracking.

RFC 9408 introduces Service Attachment Points (SAPs) for this. A SAP is an abstraction of a network reference point, such as the provider-edge side of an attachment circuit, where network services can be delivered or are already delivered to customers. A SAP can be bound to one or multiple attachment circuits.

The document does not assume any particular service. VPN services (L3VPN and L2VPN) are used only for illustration. Both User-to-Network Interface (UNI) and Network-to-Network Interface (NNI) SAPs are supported.
sections.eli5: A provider has many places where customers can connect. This document gives those places a name, SAP, so a computer can list them and decide where to hook up the next customer.

sections.title: Where the Model Sits
sections.content:
The architecture has a network controller that manages the network and a service orchestration layer above it. The controller exposes an abstracted view through the SAP network model, so the orchestrator sees which provider-edge (PE) nodes exist and which customer-facing interfaces can carry services. The orchestrator also uses customer service models such as the L3SM (RFC 8299) and L2SM (RFC 8466) towards customers, and network models such as the L3NM (RFC 9182) and L2NM (RFC 9291) towards the network.

The controller is assumed to be unaware of what lies beyond the PEs towards the customer edge (CE) equipment. To connect a delivery point in a service request to a SAP, the model may include a peer customer point identifier, such as a CE or site identifier.

The model can also expose NNIs for services that need resources from peer networks.
sections.eli5: A manager at the top asks a helper in the middle which sockets are free. The helper keeps the list but does not know what is plugged in on the customer's side of the wall.

sections.title: Relationship to Other YANG Models
sections.content:
The SAP network model can be seen as inventory data about customer-facing nodes. It augments the network model of RFC 8345 and imports its network topology model. Technology-specific topology models, such as the TE topology model and the Layer 3 topology model, augment the same topology model.

SAPs resemble customer-facing termination points, but with differences. A link is terminated by a single termination point, while an attachment circuit can be terminated by multiple SAPs. A SAP is also neither a tunnel termination point nor a link.

Advanced interface-specific data nodes are left out. The interface identifiers in the SAP model can be used as filters to get or set such data through device models.
sections.eli5: This map is built on top of an existing map of the network. It adds the sockets, but it does not describe every detail of each cable.

sections.title: The SAP Module and Its Data Nodes
sections.content:
The module ietf-sap-ntw adds a sap-network container with a list of service-type values to a network, and adds a service list to each node. Each service type holds a list of SAPs keyed by sap-id. Service types build on those defined in RFC 9181 and include L3VPN, VPLS, VPWS, EVPN variants, network slice service, SD-WAN and basic IP connectivity.

Each SAP is described by these nodes:

  • sap-id: identifies the SAP within a node. The same SAP under several service types uses the same identifier.
  • parent-termination-point: the customer-facing termination point the SAP is bound to.
  • attachment-interface, interface-type, encapsulation-type: the interface the SAP is bound to and its kind.
  • role: for example UNI or NNI, inherited from the parent interface.
  • allows-child-saps: when true, the interface can host per-service sub-interfaces.
  • peer-sap-id: references to the remote endpoints of an attachment circuit.

Two status containers report state. sap-status is the operational status of the SAP, and service-status holds the administrative and operational status of a service at that SAP.
sections.eli5: Each socket gets a label card: its name, which wall it is on, what kind of plug it takes, who is on the far end, and whether it is on or off.

sections.title: Reading Status to Spot Problems
sections.content:
The administrative service-status MUST NOT be influenced by the operational sap-status. The service oper-status reflects the service only as seen at one SAP, not the network-level state of the whole service. When both a sub-interface and its parent are present but the parent is disabled, the parent's status takes precedence.

The RFC recommends checking the administrative and operational service status together with sap-status. If a service is administratively enabled for a SAP and the SAP is reported down, the service operational status is also expected to be down. A mismatch can trigger an anomaly alert. In the other direction, a service that is administratively inactive but operationally active at a SAP signals that provisioning actions are needed to align the observed state with the expected one.
sections.eli5: There is a switch you flip on purpose and a light that shows whether power really arrives. If the switch says on but the light is off, something is wrong and someone should look.

sections.title: Examples in the Appendices
sections.content:
Appendix A shows a SAP topology in JSON encoding for the example network with PE1 to PE4 and customer equipment CE1 to CE5. SAPs able to host a service but not yet activated are marked with sap-status ietf-vpn-common:op-down and admin-down. SAPs delivering a service are marked admin-up and op-up.

Other appendices show a node filter by service type, an NNI SAP example for inter-AS VPN Option A, and how the model is used during service creation.
sections.eli5: The examples are sample label cards for a small pretend network, showing which sockets are in use and which are free.

sections.title: Security and IANA Notes
sections.content:
The module is designed to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. Their mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS respectively, and the NACM access control model can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

The writable subtree /nw:networks/nw:network/nw:node/sap:service/sap:sap is called out as sensitive. Unexpected changes, such as associating a SAP with another parent termination point, could lead to service disruption. Read access to the same subtree could disclose operational state, for example a customer identity in peer-sap-id.

IANA registered the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-sap-ntw and the module name ietf-sap-ntw with prefix sap.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should be allowed to change or even peek at the map, because moving a socket on the map could break a customer's connection.
